title: Lok Sabha Speaker extends greetings to the nation on the eve of India's 80th Independence Day
body_text:
Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla has extended greetings to the people of the country on the eve of India's 80th Independence Day.
In his message, Shri Birla has said: "Dear fellow citizens, heartfelt greetings to you all on the occasion of the 80th Independence Day.
Today is an occasion to remember the countless freedom fighters who dedicated their entire lives for independence of the country. Nearly eight decades have passed since the country gained independence, and today, we stand with a new resolve—a resolve to build a country that leads the world in every sector, driven by the potential of its youth.
Approximately 65 percent of our country's population is under the age of 35. Our youth are propelling the nation forward in education, science,
It is essential today that every young person in the country embraces our constitutional and democratic values ​​in their lives. Our youth should align their dreams with India's development and make the fulfillment of their duties a means for nation-building. On this Independence Day, let us all pledge to play our part in building a strong, self-reliant, and developed India. With this message, I once again extend my best wishes to you all for Independence Day.
Jai Hind! Jai Bharat."
* **
AM

enrichment.summary: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla issued a message greeting the nation on the eve of India's 80th Independence Day, paying tribute to freedom fighters and calling on India's youth to embrace constitutional values and contribute to building a self-reliant, developed nation. He noted that about 65 percent of India's population is under 35 years of age.
enrichment.context: This is a ceremonial greeting message issued annually by constitutional functionaries and dignitaries on the eve of Independence Day, a customary practice with no new policy announcement or decision. Such messages typically emphasize themes like national unity, the contribution of freedom fighters, and youth empowerment, often echoing government campaigns such as 'Viksit Bharat' (Developed India by 2047) and references to India's demographic dividend.
